title: No internet connection or intermittent drops
summary: The computer cannot establish network connectivity, drops offline during tasks, or connects with limited or local-only access.
symptoms: Globe icon with 'No internet access' in system tray
Webpages fail to load with DNS or timeout errors
Network connection drops every few minutes

fix_steps.title: Power cycle modem and router
fix_steps.detail: Unplug power from both modem and router for 30 seconds. Plug modem in first, wait for all status lights to stabilize, then power on router.

fix_steps.title: Run Windows Network Reset
fix_steps.detail: Go to Settings → Network & Internet → Advanced network settings → Network reset → Reset now. This reinstalls adapters and restores default network stacks.

fix_steps.title: Flush DNS and release IP configuration
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as admin and execute: 'ipconfig /flushdns', 'ipconfig /release', and 'ipconfig /renew'.

fix_steps.title: Change DNS servers to Cloudflare or Google
fix_steps.detail: In adapter properties, set IPv4 DNS manually to 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare) and 8.8.8.8 (Google) to bypass ISP DNS outages.

title: Wi-Fi shows 'Connected, no internet'
summary: The computer associates with the local wireless access point successfully, but cannot reach the default gateway or WAN upstream servers.
symptoms: Wi-Fi icon has an exclamation point or globe overlay
Network status states 'No Internet, secured'
Other devices on the same Wi-Fi can browse normally

fix_steps.title: Forget and reconnect to the Wi-Fi network
fix_steps.detail: Go to Settings → Network & Internet → Wi-Fi → Manage known networks → select your SSID → click 'Forget'. Reconnect and re-enter the WPA password.

fix_steps.title: Reset TCP/IP stack and Winsock catalog
fix_steps.detail: In administrative Command Prompt, run 'netsh int ip reset' followed by 'netsh winsock reset' and reboot the PC.

fix_steps.title: Check for invalid static IP configuration
fix_steps.detail: Open 'ncpa.cpl' → right click Wi-Fi → Properties → Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) → ensure 'Obtain an IP address automatically' and 'Obtain DNS server address automatically' are selected.

fix_steps.title: Turn off Random Hardware MAC addresses
fix_steps.detail: In Settings → Wi-Fi, disable 'Random hardware addresses'. Some routers reject DHCP leases from rotating MAC addresses.

title: Wi-Fi option missing or 'No Wi-Fi networks found'
summary: The Wi-Fi toggle disappears from the Windows taskbar, or the adapter fails to detect any surrounding wireless broadcast signals.
symptoms: Wi-Fi quick settings tile is completely missing in Windows 11
Device Manager shows yellow hazard mark on Intel Wi-Fi or Realtek Wireless adapter
Airplane mode is stuck enabled or disabled

fix_steps.title: Perform a cold power cycle (EC reset)
fix_steps.detail: Modern Intel AX200/AX210 Wi-Fi cards can enter an unrecoverable low-power state. Shut down PC, unplug power cord (or hold laptop power button for 30 seconds), wait 2 minutes, and power on.

fix_steps.title: Verify WLAN AutoConfig service is running
fix_steps.detail: Press Win+R, type 'services.msc', find 'WLAN AutoConfig'. Ensure Startup type is set to 'Automatic' and Service status is 'Running'.

fix_steps.title: Reinstall Wi-Fi adapter drivers in Device Manager
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager → Network adapters → right-click wireless adapter → Uninstall device (leave 'attempt to remove driver' unchecked) → Action → Scan for hardware changes.

fix_steps.title: Check physical Wi-Fi switch or antenna
fix_steps.detail: On desktops, ensure the external high-gain Wi-Fi antennas are screwed into the back motherboard gold SMA terminals. On laptops, verify Fn+F-key airplane toggle is off.

title: Ethernet cable plugged in but shows 'Unidentified network'
summary: Windows establishes a physical Ethernet link but fails to receive a valid DHCP lease from the router, defaulting to an unusable 169.254.x.x APIPA address.
symptoms: Ethernet icon shows yellow triangle or globe with 'Unidentified network'
Running 'ipconfig' reveals an IPv4 address starting with 169.254
Default gateway is blank in ipconfig output

fix_steps.title: Test Ethernet cable and router LAN port
fix_steps.detail: Inspect Ethernet RJ45 connectors for bent gold pins or broken locking tabs. Plug cable into a different numbered LAN port on the router, or test with a replacement CAT6 cable.

fix_steps.title: Force DHCP lease renewal
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as admin and run: 'ipconfig /release' then 'ipconfig /renew'. If it times out, the router DHCP server is unreachable.

fix_steps.title: Disable and re-enable the Ethernet network adapter
fix_steps.detail: Press Win+R, run 'ncpa.cpl', right-click 'Ethernet', select 'Disable', wait 10 seconds, then select 'Enable'.

fix_steps.title: Reinstall manufacturer LAN controller driver
fix_steps.detail: Download the latest Realtek PCIe GbE / Intel I225-V LAN driver installer from the motherboard vendor website on another device and install.

title: DNS server is not responding (DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_BAD_CONFIG)
summary: The operating system cannot translate domain names into IP addresses because the assigned DNS server is unreachable or timing out.
symptoms: Web browser shows error 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN' or 'Server IP could not be found'
Pinging numeric IPs (e.g., 'ping 1.1.1.1') works, but pinging domain names ('ping google.com') fails
Chat apps like Discord stay connected while browser websites refuse to load

fix_steps.title: Switch to public secure DNS servers
fix_steps.detail: Open Settings → Network & Internet → select your adapter → DNS server assignment → Edit → Manual → IPv4 On. Preferred DNS: 1.1.1.1, Alternate DNS: 1.0.0.1 (Cloudflare) or 8.8.8.8 (Google).

fix_steps.title: Clear the local Windows DNS cache
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as admin and execute 'ipconfig /flushdns'. Verify message 'Successfully flushed the DNS Resolver Cache'.

fix_steps.title: Restart the DNS Client service
fix_steps.detail: Run 'net stop dnscache' and 'net start dnscache' in Command Prompt, or reboot the PC.

fix_steps.title: Disable third-party VPN and DNS blockers
fix_steps.detail: Ad-blocking software (AdGuard, Pi-hole) or stale VPN configurations redirect DNS traffic to dead local loopback addresses.

title: Wi-Fi adapter displays Code 10 or Code 43 in Device Manager
summary: The operating system hardware manager halted the wireless network card because the device firmware or driver failed to initialize.
symptoms: Device Manager shows yellow warning icon next to Wi-Fi adapter
Device status: 'This device cannot start. (Code 10)' or 'Windows has stopped this device (Code 43)'
Wi-Fi toggle disappears entirely from Windows settings

fix_steps.title: Perform a complete static discharge (Drain flea power)
fix_steps.detail: Shut down PC. Disconnect AC power cord. Hold down chassis power button for 30 seconds to drain capacitors. Reconnect power and turn on. This fixes stuck firmware state in 90% of Intel Code 10 incidents.

fix_steps.title: Install clean Intel/Realtek OEM wireless drivers
fix_steps.detail: Download the standalone Wi-Fi driver from Intel or motherboard manufacturer. Uninstall existing driver with 'delete driver software' checked, reboot, and run clean installer.

fix_steps.title: Reseat M.2 Wi-Fi card inside PC/laptop
fix_steps.detail: If hardware is accessible, unscrew the M.2 2230 wireless card, clean gold contacts, reconnect tiny coaxial antenna cables firmly, and screw back into place.

fix_steps.title: Disable Fast Startup
fix_steps.detail: Fast Startup skips cold hardware resets. Disable 'Turn on fast startup' in Control Panel Power Options.

title: Wi-Fi drops connection every 10-30 minutes, especially in games
summary: The wireless connection intermittently drops packet streams or disconnects briefly due to aggressive power saving or Wi-Fi band steering conflicts.
symptoms: Sudden disconnects from Discord and multiplayer game lobbies
Ping spikes from 20ms to 999ms every few minutes
Wi-Fi reconnects automatically after 10-15 seconds

fix_steps.title: Disable adapter power saving in Device Manager
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager → Network adapters → right-click Wi-Fi adapter → Properties → Power Management tab → UNCHECK 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'.

fix_steps.title: Separate 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz Wi-Fi SSID bands on router
fix_steps.detail: Log in to router admin panel. Disable 'Smart Connect' or band steering, and create distinct SSIDs for 2.4GHz and 5GHz. Connect gaming PC solely to the 5GHz or 6GHz network.

fix_steps.title: Set Roaming Aggressiveness to Lowest
fix_steps.detail: In Device Manager → Wi-Fi adapter → Advanced tab → find 'Roaming Aggressiveness' → set value to '1. Lowest'. This stops the card from constantly scanning and dropping packets.

fix_steps.title: Set 802.11 Channel Width to 20MHz only for 2.4GHz
fix_steps.detail: Reduce channel width to 20MHz to prevent adjacent neighbor channel interference on crowded frequencies.

title: Internet blocked after disconnecting VPN (Kill Switch residue)
summary: A third-party VPN application left its virtual TAP/TUN interface or firewall kill-switch rules active upon exiting, blocking all standard network traffic.
symptoms: Internet worked while VPN was active, but completely died after turning VPN off
All browsers show connection refused or timeout
Network status says connected but zero data flows

fix_steps.title: Launch VPN and disable Kill Switch setting
fix_steps.detail: Reopen your VPN client (NordVPN, ExpressVPN, Proton, etc.), navigate to Settings → Kill Switch → toggle Off, then disconnect cleanly.

fix_steps.title: Disable virtual TAP network adapters in ncpa.cpl
fix_steps.detail: Press Win+R, type 'ncpa.cpl'. Right-click any adapters named 'TAP-Windows Adapter' or 'WireGuard Tunnel' and select 'Disable'.

fix_steps.title: Reset Windows Filtering Platform (Firewall rules)
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as admin and run: 'netsh advfirewall reset' to clear custom IP drop rules created by VPN software.

fix_steps.title: Uninstall stale VPN virtual network adapters
fix_steps.detail: In Device Manager, find Network Adapters, right-click leftover virtual VPN adapters, and select 'Uninstall device'.

title: Winsock catalog or TCP/IP stack corruption
summary: Low-level Windows network socket bindings are corrupted, preventing network socket APIs from binding ports or transmitting packet buffers.
symptoms: Browser gives error 'ERR_NETWORK_ACCESS_DENIED' or 'Socket error'
Ping works in CMD, but zero Windows applications can open web connections
Occurred following malware removal or registry cleaner usage

fix_steps.title: Execute complete Winsock catalog reset
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and execute: 'netsh winsock reset catalog'. Do not open any other apps until rebooted.

fix_steps.title: Reset IPv4 and IPv6 stacks to factory state
fix_steps.detail: In the same command prompt, run 'netsh int ip reset resetlog.txt' and 'netsh int ipv6 reset'.

fix_steps.title: Restart computer immediately
fix_steps.detail: Reboot Windows to allow the kernel network subsystem to rebuild the protocol catalog from scratch.

fix_steps.title: Verify no malicious Layered Service Providers (LSPs)
fix_steps.detail: Run 'netsh winsock show catalog' to ensure only official Microsoft kernel providers are registered.

title: 'Windows could not automatically detect network's proxy settings'
summary: A rogue browser proxy or legacy corporate PAC script is configured in Windows settings, diverting web requests into a non-existent port.
symptoms: Windows Network Troubleshooter reports 'Proxy settings issue'
Browsers display 'ERR_PROXY_CONNECTION_FAILED'
Steam or Spotify connect fine while Edge and Chrome cannot load sites

fix_steps.title: Turn off manual and automatic proxy in Windows Settings
fix_steps.detail: Go to Settings → Network & Internet → Proxy. Under 'Automatic proxy setup', turn OFF 'Automatically detect settings'. Under 'Manual proxy setup', turn OFF 'Use a proxy server'.

fix_steps.title: Inspect WinHTTP system proxy via CMD
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as admin and run: 'netsh winhttp show proxy'. If a proxy server is listed, run 'netsh winhttp reset proxy' to restore direct access.

fix_steps.title: Clean proxy entries in Windows Registry
fix_steps.detail: Navigate to 'HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings'. Set 'ProxyEnable' to 0 and delete 'ProxyServer' key.

fix_steps.title: Scan for adware with Malwarebytes
fix_steps.detail: Malicious browser hijackers install local proxy servers to inject advertisements into unencrypted HTTP traffic.

title: Gigabit Ethernet capping at 100 Mbps or 10 Mbps speed
summary: A damaged cable, dirty RJ45 port, or driver negotiation flaw restricts a Gigabit/2.5GbE connection to Fast Ethernet (100 Mbps) limits.
symptoms: Internet speed test caps at exactly 90-95 Mbps on a 500+ Mbps plan
Network connection status in Windows shows 'Link speed (Receive/Transmit): 100/100 (Mbps)'
LAN file transfers are excruciatingly slow

fix_steps.title: Replace the Ethernet cable with CAT6
fix_steps.detail: Gigabit Ethernet requires all 8 wires inside the cable. If a single pin (especially pins 4, 5, 7, 8) is severed or corroded, the NIC drops to 4-wire 100 Mbps mode.

fix_steps.title: Verify router port is Gigabit capable
fix_steps.detail: Ensure the cable is plugged into a 1Gbps or 2.5Gbps LAN port on the router, not an auxiliary 100Mbps or IPTV-designated port.

fix_steps.title: Inspect Speed & Duplex setting in Device Manager
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager → Network adapters → Ethernet adapter → Properties → Advanced tab → Speed & Duplex. Ensure it is set to 'Auto Negotiation' or '1.0 Gbps Full Duplex'.

fix_steps.title: Clean dust out of RJ45 motherboard jack
fix_steps.detail: Inspect the Ethernet port with a flashlight. Clean dust buildup on the 8 angled gold pins with compressed air or an isopropyl swab.

title: Laptop constantly switches Wi-Fi access points in mesh networks
summary: Wireless network card excessively scans and roams between mesh nodes, causing periodic micro-freezes and packet drops.
symptoms: Repeated brief 2-second voice dropouts on Zoom or Teams calls
Laptop switches between 2.4GHz and 5GHz every few minutes
Event Viewer logs continuous WLAN-AutoConfig event ID 8003

fix_steps.title: Reduce Roaming Aggressiveness to Lowest
fix_steps.detail: Device Manager → Network adapters → Intel/Realtek Wi-Fi → Properties → Advanced tab → Roaming Aggressiveness → change to 'Lowest'.

fix_steps.title: Set Preferred Band to 5GHz or 6GHz
fix_steps.detail: In the same Advanced tab, set 'Preferred Band' to '3. Prefer 5GHz band' to stop falling back to crowded 2.4GHz frequencies.

fix_steps.title: Bind device to nearest mesh satellite
fix_steps.detail: Open your mesh router app (eero, Google Nest, ASUS AiMesh) and bind your PC/laptop to the specific closest node in the room.

fix_steps.title: Update wireless adapter driver
fix_steps.detail: Modern Intel Wi-Fi drivers contain algorithm updates designed for Wi-Fi 6/6E 802.11k/v/r fast roaming protocols.

title: Network adapter stops working immediately after a Windows Update
summary: A Windows cumulative update replaced the working vendor network driver with an incompatible generic driver or corrupted adapter bindings.
symptoms: Ethernet or Wi-Fi was working before rebooting for an update
Network adapter properties show 'Driver is unavailable'
IP address shows 0.0.0.0 or configuration tab is greyed out

fix_steps.title: Roll back network driver in Device Manager
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager → Network adapters → right-click adapter → Properties → Driver tab → click 'Roll Back Driver'.

fix_steps.title: Uninstall the latest Windows Quality Update
fix_steps.detail: Go to Settings → Windows Update → Update history → Uninstall updates → find the update installed immediately prior to the failure and click 'Uninstall'.

fix_steps.title: Use manufacturer standalone offline installer
fix_steps.detail: Download the official driver installer from the motherboard vendor (Intel, Realtek, Marvell) on another PC, transfer via USB flash drive, and install.

fix_steps.title: Prevent Windows Update from replacing hardware drivers
fix_steps.detail: Open 'sysdm.cpl' → Hardware tab → Device Installation Settings → select 'No (your device might not work as expected)'.

title: Metered connection setting blocking background apps and updates
summary: Windows flagged the Wi-Fi or Ethernet connection as metered, blocking cloud synchronization, email updates, and game launcher downloads.
symptoms: Outlook and OneDrive say 'Metered Network Warning'
Steam and Epic Games refuse to download updates automatically
Windows Update pauses and prompts for manual approval

fix_steps.title: Disable Metered Connection toggle
fix_steps.detail: Go to Settings → Network & Internet → select Wi-Fi (or Ethernet) → click your network name → toggle 'Metered connection' to OFF.

fix_steps.title: Allow downloads over metered networks
fix_steps.detail: In Settings → Windows Update → Advanced options → toggle ON 'Download updates over metered connections'.

fix_steps.title: Reset network data usage limit
fix_steps.detail: Go to Settings → Network & Internet → Data usage → remove any configured monthly megabyte limits.

fix_steps.title: Restart background sync applications
fix_steps.detail: Close and reopen OneDrive, Dropbox, and cloud backup software to restore normal upload/download bandwidth.

title: IP address conflict with another system on the network
summary: Two devices on the local LAN were assigned the identical static or dynamic private IPv4 address, causing network collisions and connection drops.
symptoms: Windows balloon notification: 'There is an IP address conflict with another system on this network'
Internet immediately disconnects or alternates packets with another device
Router log shows MAC address collision for the same IP

fix_steps.title: Release and renew DHCP lease
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as admin and run 'ipconfig /release' followed by 'ipconfig /renew' to request an unused IP address from the router.

fix_steps.title: Reboot the router to clear stale DHCP tables
fix_steps.detail: Power cycle the router to flush expired DHCP lease reservations from smartphones, TVs, and IoT appliances.

fix_steps.title: Ensure PC is set to automatic DHCP
fix_steps.detail: Open 'ncpa.cpl' → adapter properties → IPv4 → verify 'Obtain an IP address automatically' is selected instead of a hardcoded static IP.

fix_steps.title: Assign an out-of-range static IP if necessary
fix_steps.detail: If you require a static IP, choose a high host number outside the router's automatic DHCP pool (e.g., 192.168.1.220).

title: IPv6 enabled on router but lacking upstream routing (20-second page load lag)
summary: Windows attempts to connect via IPv6 by default, but times out repeatedly before falling back to IPv4 (Happy Eyeballs timeout).
symptoms: Websites take 15-20 seconds before beginning to load, then load quickly
Testing on 'test-ipv6.com' results in 0/10 or broken IPv6 score
Discord and gaming connections intermittently freeze on connecting

fix_steps.title: Disable Internet Protocol Version 6 (TCP/IPv6) on the adapter
fix_steps.detail: Press Win+R, type 'ncpa.cpl'. Right-click your active network adapter → Properties → UNCHECK 'Internet Protocol Version 6 (TCP/IPv6)' → click OK.

fix_steps.title: Configure IPv4 preference over IPv6 via registry
fix_steps.detail: Microsoft provides an official wizard to prefer IPv4 over IPv6 in prefix policies, eliminating lookup timeouts.

fix_steps.title: Check router IPv6 WAN settings
fix_steps.detail: Log in to your router. If your ISP does not provide native IPv6 routing, toggle IPv6 to Disabled on the router WAN interface.

fix_steps.title: Flush DNS resolver cache
fix_steps.detail: Run 'ipconfig /flushdns' in Command Prompt to purge cached AAAA (IPv6) DNS resource records.

title: The default gateway is not available (yellow exclamation mark)
summary: The network adapter loses route connectivity to the local router or access point, causing Windows network diagnostics to continually reset the gateway adapter.
symptoms: Windows Troubleshooter reports: 'The default gateway is not available - Fixed', but it breaks again 10 minutes later
Yellow warning triangle on taskbar network icon
Cannot access local router web interface at 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1

fix_steps.title: Disable network adapter power management sleep
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager > Network adapters > Right-click your Wi-Fi or Ethernet adapter > Properties > Power Management tab > Uncheck 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' > Click OK.

fix_steps.title: Assign a static Default Gateway and IP address
fix_steps.detail: Open ncpa.cpl > Right-click network adapter > Properties > Double-click Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) > Set manual IP: 192.168.1.150, Subnet: 255.255.255.0, Gateway: 192.168.1.1, DNS: 1.1.1.1.

fix_steps.title: Perform full network stack reset in CMD
fix_steps.detail: Run in Administrator Command Prompt: netsh int ip reset && netsh winsock reset && ipconfig /flushdns, then restart the computer.

fix_steps.title: Update router firmware and check for IP lease exhaustion
fix_steps.detail: Log in to your router admin panel. Increase the DHCP IP pool range or update the router firmware to resolve ARP table dropouts.

title: Wi-Fi 6E / 7 (6 GHz band) SSID not showing in Windows 11
summary: Intel AX210/AX211 or Qualcomm Wi-Fi 6E adapters fail to broadcast or detect 6 GHz SSIDs due to outdated drivers, regional regulatory domain locks, or WPA3 requirement mismatches.
symptoms: Router broadcasts 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz, but 6 GHz network is completely invisible in Windows
Smartphones connect to the 6 GHz Wi-Fi 6E network without issues in the same room
Wi-Fi adapter is verified as Wi-Fi 6E capable in Device Manager

fix_steps.title: Update to the latest Intel PROSet / Wireless Wi-Fi driver
fix_steps.detail: Download the latest Wi-Fi driver directly from Intel Driver & Support Assistant. Driver versions older than 22.190 frequently disable 6 GHz discovery in Windows 11.

fix_steps.title: Ensure router security is set strictly to WPA3-Personal
fix_steps.detail: The Wi-Fi 6E specification requires WPA3 encryption. In router wireless settings, change the 6 GHz security mode from 'WPA2/WPA3 Mixed' to pure 'WPA3-Personal (AES)'.

fix_steps.title: Enable 802.11ax / WiFi 6E Mode in Device Manager
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager > Network adapters > Intel Wi-Fi 6E adapter > Properties > Advanced tab > Ensure '802.11ax / 6GHz Band' is set to Enabled.

fix_steps.title: Upgrade Windows 10 to Windows 11
fix_steps.detail: Microsoft and Intel restrict native 6 GHz Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 band access to Windows 11 Build 22000 and newer. Windows 10 lacks official 6 GHz regulatory support.

title: Intel I225-V and I226-V Ethernet micro-drops connection while gaming
summary: The 2.5 GbE Intel I225-V and I226-V onboard Ethernet controllers suffer from hardware packet buffer drops when Energy Efficient Ethernet (EEE) powers down the PHY transceiver.
symptoms: Ethernet connection drops for 2-3 seconds and reconnects during multiplayer games or Discord calls
Event Viewer shows e2fnexpress Event ID 27: 'Intel Ethernet Controller network link is disconnected'
Affects Intel Z690, Z790, and B650 / X670 motherboards with 2.5G ports

fix_steps.title: Disable Energy Efficient Ethernet (EEE) in adapter settings
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager > Network adapters > Intel Ethernet Controller > Properties > Advanced tab > Scroll to 'Energy Efficient Ethernet' and set to Disabled.

fix_steps.title: Disable Ultra Low Power Mode and Green Ethernet
fix_steps.detail: In the same Advanced tab, set 'Ultra Low Power Mode' to Disabled, and set 'Green Ethernet' to Disabled.

fix_steps.title: Force Link Speed to 1.0 Gbps Full Duplex
fix_steps.detail: If connecting to a 1 Gbps Gigabit home router, change 'Speed & Duplex' from 'Auto Negotiation' to '1.0 Gbps Full Duplex' to prevent continuous negotiation renegotiation.

fix_steps.title: Install Intel NVM Firmware Update from motherboard support
fix_steps.detail: Visit your motherboard support page and download the 'Intel I225/I226 NVM Firmware Update tool' to flash the onboard network controller microcode.

title: Wi-Fi does not have a valid IP configuration (169.254.x.x APIPA)
summary: The computer connects to the wireless router radio but fails to receive a DHCP IP address lease, defaulting to an unroutable 169.254.x.x Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) address.
symptoms: Windows network troubleshooter reports 'Wi-Fi does not have a valid IP configuration'
Running ipconfig shows IPv4 Address: 169.254.x.x and empty Default Gateway
Wi-Fi status reports 'No Internet, secured'

fix_steps.title: Release and renew IP address lease in Command Prompt
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and execute: ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew. If it reports 'unable to contact DHCP server', proceed to reset services.

fix_steps.title: Restart the DHCP Client service
fix_steps.detail: Press Win + R, type 'services.msc', find 'DHCP Client', confirm its status is 'Running', and ensure its Startup Type is set to Automatic.

fix_steps.title: Reboot home router to clear full DHCP table
fix_steps.detail: Unplug your internet modem and Wi-Fi router from the wall outlet for 30 seconds, plug them back in, and wait 2 minutes for the router DHCP pool to reinitialize.

fix_steps.title: Forget and reconnect to the Wi-Fi network
fix_steps.detail: Go to Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks > Click 'Forget' next to your network name > Reconnect and enter the Wi-Fi password freshly.

title: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi speed drops drastically when Bluetooth is turned on
summary: The single Wi-Fi/Bluetooth combo card shares one internal antenna, causing packet collisions between Bluetooth audio/peripherals and 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi bands.
symptoms: Wi-Fi speed drops from 50 Mbps down to 2 Mbps whenever Bluetooth headphones or mouse are connected
Audio cuts out or crackles when downloading files over Wi-Fi
Turning off Bluetooth in Windows settings immediately restores normal Wi-Fi speeds

fix_steps.title: Connect to your router 5 GHz or 6 GHz Wi-Fi band
fix_steps.detail: Open Wi-Fi settings and connect to your router 5 GHz network (often named NetworkName_5G). 5 GHz is completely immune to 2.4 GHz Bluetooth radio interference.

fix_steps.title: Enable Bluetooth AMP / Coexistence in Advanced adapter settings
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager > Network adapters > Right-click Wi-Fi card > Properties > Advanced > Set 'Bluetooth AMP' or 'Coexistence Support' to Enabled.

fix_steps.title: Change 2.4 GHz channel width in router settings to 20 MHz
fix_steps.detail: Log in to your router settings, navigate to 2.4 GHz wireless, and change Channel Bandwidth from '40 MHz' to '20 MHz' to reduce spectral overlap with Bluetooth frequency hopping.

fix_steps.title: Screw in external motherboard magnetic shark-fin antenna
fix_steps.detail: If using a desktop PC, ensure the dual-wire antenna included with the motherboard is screwed securely into the rear golden coaxial RP-SMA connectors.

title: Network profile stuck on Public blocking network printer and file sharing
summary: Windows sets the network profile type to Public by default, activating strict Windows Defender Firewall rules that block local printer discovery, SMB shares, and ping requests.
symptoms: Network printer shows 'Offline' even though other devices can print
Cannot access shared folders (\\PCNAME) across the home network
Network profile toggle missing or greyed out in Windows Settings

fix_steps.title: Change network profile to Private in Windows Settings
fix_steps.detail: Go to Settings > Network & internet > Click 'Wi-Fi' or 'Ethernet' > Click your connected network name > Under Network profile type, select 'Private network'.

fix_steps.title: Change profile to Private using PowerShell
fix_steps.detail: Open PowerShell as Administrator and run: Get-NetConnectionProfile. Note the InterfaceAlias name and execute: Set-NetConnectionProfile -Name 'YourNetworkName' -NetworkCategory Private.

fix_steps.title: Enable Network Discovery and File Sharing
fix_steps.detail: Go to Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Advanced sharing settings > Under Private networks, toggle 'Network discovery' and 'File and printer sharing' to ON.

fix_steps.title: Restart Function Discovery services in services.msc
fix_steps.detail: Open services.msc and set 'Function Discovery Provider Host' and 'Function Discovery Resource Publication' Startup Types to Automatic and start both.

title: Captive portal hotel / airport Wi-Fi login splash page not loading
summary: The browser fails to open the hotel, café, or airport authentication redirect page because third-party DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH), VPNs, or HSTS security headers block cleartext HTTP interception.
symptoms: Connected to public Wi-Fi with 'No internet, open' status
Opening browser shows 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NO_INTERNET' instead of hotel login page
Network prompt 'Action needed' fails to load login screen

fix_steps.title: Navigate to cleartext neverssl.com in browser
fix_steps.detail: Open your web browser and type: http://neverssl.com into the address bar. Because this site uses unencrypted HTTP without HSTS, the captive portal router will easily intercept and display the login screen.

fix_steps.title: Temporarily turn off VPN software
fix_steps.detail: Disconnect and fully exit VPN applications (NordVPN, ExpressVPN, Tailscale, Cloudflare WARP). VPN kill-switches block all unencrypted portal redirect gateways.

fix_steps.title: Disable DNS-over-HTTPS (Secure DNS) in browser
fix_steps.detail: In Chrome/Edge settings, search for 'Secure DNS' or 'Use secure DNS' and toggle it off temporarily so local hotel DNS servers can intercept domain requests.

fix_steps.title: Type default gateway router IP directly into address bar
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt, run ipconfig, note the Default Gateway (e.g. 192.168.0.1 or 10.0.0.1), and type http://[Default_Gateway_IP] directly into your browser address bar.

title: Network card remains asleep and disconnected after computer wakes
summary: Windows Power Management puts the PCIe network interface card (NIC) into D3hot power state during sleep, but the device driver fails to restore D0 operating state upon wake.
symptoms: Internet works perfectly on cold boot, but stays disconnected every time the PC wakes from sleep
Network icon shows a red X or globe for 60 seconds after waking
Requires disabling and re-enabling the network adapter in Control Panel to restore connection

fix_steps.title: Disable Fast Startup in Windows Control Panel
fix_steps.detail: Press Win + R, type 'powercfg.cpl', click 'Choose what the power buttons do', click 'Change settings that are currently unavailable', uncheck 'Turn on fast startup', and click Save changes.

fix_steps.title: Disable selective suspend and adapter sleep settings
fix_steps.detail: In Device Manager, open Network adapters > Right-click NIC > Properties > Advanced tab > Disable 'Energy Efficient Ethernet', 'Green Ethernet', and 'System Idle Power Saver'.

fix_steps.title: Turn off Energy-Saving Ethernet in Device Power Management
fix_steps.detail: In the same Properties window, open the 'Power Management' tab and uncheck 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'.

fix_steps.title: Install OEM driver package over generic Windows Update driver
fix_steps.detail: Windows Update provides basic generic Microsoft-packaged drivers that lack proper PCIe D-state power transition firmware. Download the full driver installer from Realtek or Intel.

title: Ethernet speed capped at 100 Mbps instead of 1 Gbps (1000 Mbps)
summary: Paying for 300Mbps to 1Gbps internet but Windows Ethernet link speed shows capped at 100/100 Mbps.
symptoms: Windows Network Properties shows 'Link speed (Receive/Transmit): 100/100 (Mbps)'
Speed test never exceeds 94-95 Mbps on a 500Mbps+ fiber plan
Ethernet port LED shows amber/orange instead of green

fix_steps.title: Inspect and replace damaged Cat5/Cat5e Ethernet cable
fix_steps.instruction: Gigabit Ethernet (1000 Mbps) requires all 8 copper pins to negotiate properly. If even one pin is bent or severed, Windows falls back to 4-pin Fast Ethernet (100 Mbps). Swap cable for a certified Cat6 patch cable.
fix_steps.caution: Avoid flat or ultra-thin ribbon Ethernet cables over long runs due to crosstalk.
fix_steps.detail: Gigabit Ethernet (1000 Mbps) requires all 8 copper pins to negotiate properly. If even one pin is bent or severed, Windows falls back to 4-pin Fast Ethernet (100 Mbps). Swap cable for a certified Cat6 patch cable.

fix_steps.title: Disable Energy Efficient Ethernet and Green Ethernet
fix_steps.instruction: Open Device Manager -> Network adapters -> right-click your Intel/Realtek Ethernet controller -> Properties -> Advanced tab. Set 'Energy Efficient Ethernet', 'Green Ethernet', and 'Gigabit Lite' to 'Disabled'.
fix_steps.caution: Power saving features cause Realtek NICs to downshift link speed.
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager -> Network adapters -> right-click your Intel/Realtek Ethernet controller -> Properties -> Advanced tab. Set 'Energy Efficient Ethernet', 'Green Ethernet', and 'Gigabit Lite' to 'Disabled'.

fix_steps.title: Force Speed & Duplex to 1.0 Gbps Full Duplex
fix_steps.instruction: In the same Advanced tab, find 'Speed & Duplex'. If set to 'Auto Negotiation' and negotiating 100 Mbps, test setting it explicitly to '1.0 Gbps Full Duplex'. Click OK.
fix_steps.caution: If the link completely drops when forced to 1.0 Gbps, the physical cable or wall port jack is physically damaged.
fix_steps.detail: In the same Advanced tab, find 'Speed & Duplex'. If set to 'Auto Negotiation' and negotiating 100 Mbps, test setting it explicitly to '1.0 Gbps Full Duplex'. Click OK.

title: Internet completely dies whenever VPN is disconnected or uninstalled
summary: Browser cannot open any websites after disconnecting from NordVPN, ExpressVPN, or ProtonVPN.
symptoms: Internet works while connected to VPN, but immediately dies when VPN is turned off
Browser reports 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NO_INTERNET'
VPN Kill-Switch remained engaged in Windows network stack

fix_steps.title: Reopen VPN client and turn off 'Kill Switch'
fix_steps.instruction: Launch your VPN app (NordVPN, Proton, Express, Mullvad). Go to Settings -> Connection / Security -> toggle OFF 'Kill Switch' and 'Block non-VPN traffic'. Disconnect properly from within the app.
fix_steps.caution: Force-closing a VPN via Task Manager leaves its Windows firewall filter rules active.
fix_steps.detail: Launch your VPN app (NordVPN, Proton, Express, Mullvad). Go to Settings -> Connection / Security -> toggle OFF 'Kill Switch' and 'Block non-VPN traffic'. Disconnect properly from within the app.

fix_steps.title: Reset Windows Firewall and TAP adapters
fix_steps.instruction: Open Windows Defender Firewall -> click 'Restore defaults' on the left sidebar. Then open Device Manager -> Network adapters -> right-click any virtual 'TAP-Windows Adapter' or 'Wintun Userspace Tunnel' -> Uninstall device.
fix_steps.caution: Windows will cleanly regenerate standard network routes on reboot.
fix_steps.detail: Open Windows Defender Firewall -> click 'Restore defaults' on the left sidebar. Then open Device Manager -> Network adapters -> right-click any virtual 'TAP-Windows Adapter' or 'Wintun Userspace Tunnel' -> Uninstall device.

fix_steps.title: Flush DNS and reset TCP/IP and Winsock catalog
fix_steps.instruction: Open Command Prompt as Administrator. Run: 'netsh winsock reset', 'netsh int ip reset', 'ipconfig /release', 'ipconfig /flushdns', 'ipconfig /renew'. Reboot PC.
fix_steps.caution: Reboot is required for the Winsock reset to take effect.
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as Administrator. Run: 'netsh winsock reset', 'netsh int ip reset', 'ipconfig /release', 'ipconfig /flushdns', 'ipconfig /renew'. Reboot PC.

title: Wi-Fi ping spikes to 300ms+ every 60 seconds during online gaming
summary: Gaming has steady 20ms ping that spikes to 300ms-1000ms every 60 seconds due to Windows background Wi-Fi scanning.
symptoms: Ping spikes in Valorant, CS2, Fortnite, or Rocket League exactly every 60 seconds
Command Prompt 'ping 1.1.1.1 -t' shows 15ms with periodic 400ms jumps
Windows WLAN AutoConfig background roaming scan active

fix_steps.title: Disable background Wi-Fi network scanning with WLAN Optimizer or netsh
fix_steps.instruction: Windows scans for nearby Wi-Fi networks every 60 seconds, which freezes game packets. Open Command Prompt (Admin) and run: 'netsh wlan set autoconfig enabled=no interface="Wi-Fi"'.
fix_steps.caution: To search for new Wi-Fi networks in the future, re-enable with: 'netsh wlan set autoconfig enabled=yes interface="Wi-Fi"'.
fix_steps.detail: Windows scans for nearby Wi-Fi networks every 60 seconds, which freezes game packets. Open Command Prompt (Admin) and run: 'netsh wlan set autoconfig enabled=no interface="Wi-Fi"'.

fix_steps.title: Switch Wi-Fi adapter to 5 GHz band exclusively
fix_steps.instruction: In Device Manager -> Network adapters -> Wi-Fi card -> Properties -> Advanced. Set 'Preferred Band' to 'Prefer 5GHz Band' and 'Channel Width for 5GHz' to 'Auto'.
fix_steps.caution: 2.4 GHz is crowded with microwave ovens and Bluetooth interference.
fix_steps.detail: In Device Manager -> Network adapters -> Wi-Fi card -> Properties -> Advanced. Set 'Preferred Band' to 'Prefer 5GHz Band' and 'Channel Width for 5GHz' to 'Auto'.

fix_steps.title: Disable Roaming Aggressiveness
fix_steps.instruction: In the same Advanced tab, set 'Roaming Aggressiveness' to '1. Lowest'. This stops your PC from constantly hunting for other mesh router nodes.
fix_steps.caution: Keep at lowest if PC is stationary at a desk.
fix_steps.detail: In the same Advanced tab, set 'Roaming Aggressiveness' to '1. Lowest'. This stops your PC from constantly hunting for other mesh router nodes.

title: DNS server not responding: switching to Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) and Google (8.8.8.8)
summary: Websites fail to load with 'Server IP address could not be found' while ping to 8.8.8.8 works fine.
symptoms: Browser reports 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_BAD_CONFIG' or 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN'
Discord or Steam works, but Chrome and Edge cannot open any web pages
ISP default DNS server timing out or intercepting queries

fix_steps.title: Set manual IPv4 DNS to Cloudflare and Google
fix_steps.instruction: Press Win+R, type 'ncpa.cpl' and press Enter. Right-click your active network connection -> Properties. Select 'Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4)' -> click Properties. Check 'Use the following DNS server addresses': Preferred DNS: 1.1.1.1, Alternate DNS: 8.8.8.8. Click OK.
fix_steps.caution: Do not alter the IP address settings above DNS.
fix_steps.detail: Press Win+R, type 'ncpa.cpl' and press Enter. Right-click your active network connection -> Properties. Select 'Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4)' -> click Properties. Check 'Use the following DNS server addresses': Preferred DNS: 1.1.1.1, Alternate DNS: 8.8.8.8. Click OK.

fix_steps.title: Configure Encrypted DNS (DNS over HTTPS) in Windows 11
fix_steps.instruction: Open Windows Settings -> Network & internet -> Wi-Fi or Ethernet -> Hardware properties. Under DNS server assignment, click 'Edit' -> choose 'Manual' -> toggle IPv4 ON -> set Preferred DNS to 1.1.1.1 and DNS encryption to 'Encrypted only (DNS over HTTPS)'.
fix_steps.caution: Encrypts all domain lookups to prevent ISP spying and DNS hijacking.
fix_steps.detail: Open Windows Settings -> Network & internet -> Wi-Fi or Ethernet -> Hardware properties. Under DNS server assignment, click 'Edit' -> choose 'Manual' -> toggle IPv4 ON -> set Preferred DNS to 1.1.1.1 and DNS encryption to 'Encrypted only (DNS over HTTPS)'.

fix_steps.title: Flush Windows DNS resolver cache
fix_steps.instruction: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run: 'ipconfig /flushdns'. Verify output confirms 'Successfully flushed the DNS Resolver Cache.'
fix_steps.caution: Restart your browser to clear internal browser DNS sockets.
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run: 'ipconfig /flushdns'. Verify output confirms 'Successfully flushed the DNS Resolver Cache.'

title: 5GHz Wi-Fi network not showing up in Windows while phone connects fine
summary: Dual-band router broadcasts 5GHz Wi-Fi, but PC only sees 2.4GHz network or cannot find SSID.
symptoms: Phone and tablet see the 5GHz network, but PC only lists the slow 2.4GHz network
Wi-Fi card supports 802.11ac / 802.11ax but fails to detect 5GHz channels
Router configured with DFS channels (Channels 52-144) unsupported by PC card

fix_steps.title: Change router 5GHz channel from DFS to standard channel 36 or 149
fix_steps.instruction: Log in to your Wi-Fi router admin page (e.g. 192.168.1.1). Navigate to Wireless 5GHz settings. Change Channel from 'Auto' to Channel 36, 40, 44, or 149. Avoid DFS channels (52 to 144) which many PC Wi-Fi cards ignore.
fix_steps.caution: DFS channels require radar checking and cause disconnects near airports.
fix_steps.detail: Log in to your Wi-Fi router admin page (e.g. 192.168.1.1). Navigate to Wireless 5GHz settings. Change Channel from 'Auto' to Channel 36, 40, 44, or 149. Avoid DFS channels (52 to 144) which many PC Wi-Fi cards ignore.

fix_steps.title: Set Wireless Mode to 802.11a/n/ac in Device Manager
fix_steps.instruction: Open Device Manager -> Network adapters -> right-click Wi-Fi adapter -> Properties -> Advanced. Set 'Wireless Mode' to '802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax' (dual-band mode) instead of '2.4GHz only'.
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager -> Network adapters -> right-click Wi-Fi adapter -> Properties -> Advanced. Set 'Wireless Mode' to '802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax' (dual-band mode) instead of '2.4GHz only'.

fix_steps.title: Separate 2.4GHz and 5GHz SSIDs in router
fix_steps.instruction: If your router uses 'Smart Connect' / band steering (single SSID for both bands), turn it off. Name them separately: 'MyHome_2.4G' and 'MyHome_5G'. Manually connect PC to 'MyHome_5G'.
fix_steps.caution: Band steering frequently drops PCs to 2.4GHz when signal drops slightly.
fix_steps.detail: If your router uses 'Smart Connect' / band steering (single SSID for both bands), turn it off. Name them separately: 'MyHome_2.4G' and 'MyHome_5G'. Manually connect PC to 'MyHome_5G'.

title: Steam download speeds crawling or dropping to 0 KB/s on fast fiber internet
summary: Steam downloads fluctuate wildly or stop completely while Task Manager shows 100% disk usage.
symptoms: Steam download graph shows green disk line dropping to 0 MB/s
Download fluctuates between 50 MB/s and 0 KB/s repeatedly
Speedtest shows 500Mbps, but Steam takes 3 hours for a 20GB game

fix_steps.title: Clear Steam download cache
fix_steps.instruction: In Steam, click Steam (top left) -> Settings -> Downloads. Click 'Clear Download Cache' -> Confirm. Steam will restart and prompt you to log back in.
fix_steps.caution: Wipes stuck fragmented chunk files without touching installed games.
fix_steps.detail: In Steam, click Steam (top left) -> Settings -> Downloads. Click 'Clear Download Cache' -> Confirm. Steam will restart and prompt you to log back in.

fix_steps.title: Switch Steam Download Region to nearby high-capacity server
fix_steps.instruction: In Steam Settings -> Downloads -> 'Download Region'. If set to an overloaded local server, switch to a neighboring major hub (e.g. Singapore, Frankfurt, or Chicago).
fix_steps.caution: Steam does not lock matchmaking to download region; you can change this freely.
fix_steps.detail: In Steam Settings -> Downloads -> 'Download Region'. If set to an overloaded local server, switch to a neighboring major hub (e.g. Singapore, Frankfurt, or Chicago).

fix_steps.title: Exclude Steam library folder from Windows Defender real-time scanning
fix_steps.instruction: Open Windows Security -> Virus & threat protection -> Manage settings -> Exclusions (Add an exclusion) -> Folder. Select your 'steamapps' folder. Windows Defender scans every compressed block as Steam unpacks it, maxing out your CPU.
fix_steps.caution: Only exclude official Steam library folders where verified games reside.
fix_steps.detail: Open Windows Security -> Virus & threat protection -> Manage settings -> Exclusions (Add an exclusion) -> Folder. Select your 'steamapps' folder. Windows Defender scans every compressed block as Steam unpacks it, maxing out your CPU.

title: Intel Wi-Fi 6/6E/7 (AX200/AX210/BE200) Code 10/43 Driver Reset Loop
summary: Fix Intel Wi-Fi 6 (AX200/AX201), Wi-Fi 6E (AX210/AX211), and Wi-Fi 7 (BE200) adapters throwing Device Manager Code 10 or Code 43 reset loops.
symptoms: Wi-Fi adapter displays yellow exclamation mark in Device Manager with Code 10 or Code 43
Wi-Fi toggle switch completely disappears from Windows 10/11 taskbar and Settings
Windows Event Viewer System log displays repeated Netwtw10 or Netwtw14 Event IDs 5002, 5005, and 5007

fix_steps.title: Perform cold hardware EC discharge
fix_steps.detail: Shut down PC, unplug AC power cable from PSU, and hold down chassis power button for a full 30 to 45 seconds to drain all residual charge from motherboard capacitors and force Wi-Fi card embedded controller reset.

fix_steps.title: Download latest standalone Intel PROSet Wi-Fi driver
fix_steps.detail: On a phone or secondary PC, download latest Intel Wireless Wi-Fi Drivers for Windows 10 and Windows 11 package from official Intel Download Center.

fix_steps.title: Clean uninstall wireless device
fix_steps.detail: In Device Manager, expand Network adapters, right-click Intel Wi-Fi adapter, click Uninstall device, check Attempt to remove the driver for this device, and click Uninstall.

fix_steps.title: Disable adapter power saving in Device Manager
fix_steps.detail: After installing new driver, right-click adapter in Device Manager -> Properties -> Power Management -> uncheck Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power.

title: MediaTek and Realtek Wi-Fi PCIe ASPM Sleep State Wake Hang Triage
summary: Resolve MediaTek MT7921/MT7922 and Realtek RTL8852AE/BE Wi-Fi cards failing to reconnect or disappearing from Device Manager after PC wakes from sleep.
symptoms: Wi-Fi disconnects immediately when laptop or PC wakes up from sleep or Modern Standby
Wi-Fi card vanishes from Device Manager until system is completely shut down and powered back on
Bluetooth continues working while Wi-Fi component reports hardware failure

fix_steps.title: Disable PCIe Link State Power Management
fix_steps.detail: Open Windows Control Panel -> Power Options -> Edit Plan Settings -> Change advanced power settings -> PCI Express -> Link State Power Management -> set both On battery and Plugged in to Off.

fix_steps.title: Disable adapter sleep state power savings
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager -> Network adapters -> right-click MediaTek or Realtek wireless adapter -> Properties -> Power Management -> uncheck Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power.

fix_steps.title: Install latest OEM manufacturer driver
fix_steps.detail: Download updated Wi-Fi drivers from your laptop manufacturer (ASUS, Lenovo, HP) support website rather than relying on standard Microsoft Windows Update drivers.

fix_steps.title: Reseat M.2 2230 Wi-Fi card in slot
fix_steps.detail: On desktop motherboards or accessible laptops, remove M.2 Wi-Fi card, clean gold contacts with isopropyl alcohol, and reseat firmly with antenna connectors locked securely.

title: Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) Multi-Link Operation MLO Packet Loss and Disconnects
summary: Diagnose packet drops, high jitter, and roaming disconnections on Wi-Fi 7 routers with Multi-Link Operation (MLO) enabled across 2.4GHz, 5GHz, and 6GHz bands.
symptoms: Severe gaming ping spikes and intermittent 2-second packet drops on Wi-Fi 7 router
Connection drops and reconnects frequently while streaming or video conferencing
Wi-Fi link speed fluctuates wildly between 200Mbps and 2400Mbps

fix_steps.title: Update Windows 11 to Build 24H2 or newer
fix_steps.detail: Native Multi-Link Operation (MLO) protocol support requires Windows 11 Version 24H2 or later. Check winver to ensure OS is updated with official Wi-Fi 7 client stack support.

fix_steps.title: Split Wi-Fi 7 SSIDs or disable MLO on router
fix_steps.detail: Log into router administration portal, locate Wi-Fi 7 / MLO settings, and temporarily disable MLO or assign separate SSIDs to 5GHz and 6GHz bands to eliminate band steering conflicts.

fix_steps.title: Update client Wi-Fi card driver
fix_steps.detail: Install the latest Intel BE200 or Qualcomm Wi-Fi 7 driver package directly from the chip manufacturer to patch early firmware link-aggregation bugs.

fix_steps.title: Lower 6GHz channel bandwidth to 160MHz
fix_steps.detail: In router 6GHz wireless settings, reduce channel width from 320MHz to 160MHz if physical obstacles or neighborhood interference cause high packet error rates on 320MHz channels.

title: DHCP 169.254 Self-Assigned APIPA IP Address Resolution
summary: Isolate and fix Windows defaulting to an Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) 169.254.x.x address when the DHCP server fails to respond to lease requests.
symptoms: Network status shows yellow triangle with: No internet access or Unidentified network
Running ipconfig reveals Autoconfiguration IPv4 Address starting with 169.254
Default Gateway is completely blank in ipconfig output

fix_steps.title: Release and renew DHCP address lease
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run: ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew to re-broadcast DHCP discovery packets across the local subnet.

fix_steps.title: Restart Windows DHCP Client service
fix_steps.detail: Press Win+R, type services.msc, locate DHCP Client service, verify Status is Running and Startup Type is Automatic. If greyed out, restart PC.

fix_steps.title: Power cycle local router and switches
fix_steps.detail: Unplug power to your router and any intermediate network switches, wait 30 seconds, and plug back in to clear corrupted DHCP lease tables.

fix_steps.title: Test temporary manual static IP address
fix_steps.detail: Open Network Connections -> right-click adapter -> Properties -> IPv4 Properties -> choose Use the following IP address -> enter 192.168.1.185 (or matching subnet), Subnet 255.255.255.0, Gateway 192.168.1.1, DNS 1.1.1.1.

title: Router DHCP IP Address Pool Exhaustion and Static IP Allocation
summary: Diagnose network connections failing due to router DHCP lease scope exhaustion from smart home and mobile devices, and assign static IP leases.
symptoms: Newly connected or rebooted PC cannot get an IP address, while already-connected devices work fine
Wi-Fi connects but states: Connected, no internet, obtaining IP address stuck
Router administrative log contains warnings: DHCP pool exhausted

fix_steps.title: Check active DHCP leases in router portal
fix_steps.detail: Open web browser, navigate to router gateway IP (usually 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1), log in with admin credentials, and open DHCP Client List / Connected Devices.

fix_steps.title: Widen DHCP IP address range
fix_steps.detail: In router LAN / DHCP settings, expand the starting and ending IP pool range (e.g. expand from 192.168.1.100-192.168.1.150 up to 192.168.1.20-192.168.1.240) to accommodate more client devices.

fix_steps.title: Reduce DHCP lease duration
fix_steps.detail: Shorten DHCP lease time setting from default 7 days to 24 hours or 12 hours so abandoned leases from guest phones and transient devices are reclaimed promptly.

fix_steps.title: Create static DHCP reservation for PC
fix_steps.detail: In router DHCP reservation table, add your computer MAC address and bind it to a dedicated static IP address outside the dynamic pool (e.g. 192.168.1.50).

title: Winsock Catalog and TCP/IP Protocol Stack Reset Triage
summary: Rebuild corrupted Windows Sockets (Winsock) catalog, Layered Service Providers (LSP), and TCP/IP protocol stack after malware removal or network update.
symptoms: Web browser displays ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED or The connection was reset on all websites
Cannot ping local router IP address or internet DNS despite adapter reporting active link
Network stack corrupted following VPN removal or third-party firewall uninstallation

fix_steps.title: Reset Winsock catalog
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and execute: netsh winsock reset. This cleans out third-party Layered Service Providers (LSPs) that intercept socket traffic.

fix_steps.title: Reset TCP/IP protocol stack
fix_steps.detail: In the same Administrator command prompt, execute: netsh int ip reset c:\resetlog.txt. This resets TCP/IP registry parameters back to default Windows values.

fix_steps.title: Flush and re-register DNS client resolver
fix_steps.detail: Execute commands: ipconfig /flushdns followed by ipconfig /registerdns to clear cached name resolutions.

fix_steps.title: Execute complete Windows Network Reset
fix_steps.detail: If commands fail, open Windows Settings -> Network & internet -> Advanced network settings -> Network reset -> click Reset now. Windows will reinstall all network adapters and reboot.
